To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-3 is required to increase blood basophils during infection with N.b. (or S.v.), and IL-3 can enhance IL-4 production in vitro by basophils activated with anti-Ig.
IL-3 is required to increase the number of basophils in the circulation of infected mice, and IL-3 enhances the production of IL-4 by activated basophils.
IL-3 is required to increase the numbers of blood and bone marrow basophila during infection of mice and can enhance IL-4 production in response to anti-IgE stimulation in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL-3 and basophils in regulating the immune response eliciting by nematode infection.
the role of IL-3 in regulating the numbers of basophils in blood and other tissues, and the ability of basophils to produce IL- 4, during infection of mice by nematode parasites.
the regulation of basophils during the immune response to N.b. infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data presented in this study show that IL-3 is required to increase blood basophil levels in nematode infections in mice and can also enhance IL-4 production from these basophils in response to anti-IgE stimulation.
IL-3 is required to induce basophilia during nematode infection, and can enhance Ig-dependent IL-4 expression in basophils in vivo.
IL-3 is required to induce basophil expansion and to enhance IL-4 production in response to IgE-mediated stimulation in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-3 is an important regulator of basophils in infection with N. brasiliensis and can enhance Ig E-dependent IL-4 secretion by basophils.

IL-3 is required in mice to increase basophils in the blood and bone marrow in response to infection with N. brasiliensis or S. venezuelensis, and IL-3 also can enhance IL-4 production from these basophils in response to anti-IgE.
IL-3 is required to maintain basophils in the blood during nematode infections, and that IL-3 enhances the production of IL-4 by these basophils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-3 can enhance the ability of basophils to produce IL- 4 after stimulation with IgE and anti-IgE.
IL-3 can enhance the numbers and function of basophils in vivo, which may be important during immune responses in mice, and perhaps also in humans.
IL-3 is required to increase the numbers of blood and bone marrow basophila during nematode infection, and that IL-3 can enhance IgE-mediated IL-4 production in vitro.
